 AMD is a 'data center first' company, says CEO Lisa Su

 Learn more AMD ( AMD ) CEO Lisa Su sits down with Yahoo Finance's Executive Editor Brian Sozzi to discuss rapid AI adoption driving massive data center demand, address Wall Street's short-term skepticism over hyperscaler spending, and explain why sustained investments in computing power are essential for long-term growth. 
 Video Transcript 00:00 Brian You've come out a couple times this year with some really like a really strong outlook. And you know, on the third quarter earnings call, this was no no like no exception. I mean, strong outlook, you're highlighting strong demand for for data centers. Like what is surprising you in terms of demand? Because of course, you know, the CEO sits with the CFO and the team and they, you know, work out an outlook and they plan and they scenario plan. Something is surprising to the upside in a big way for a company like AMD. What is it? 
 00:35 Lisa Well, I think what we're seeing, Brian is the following. Um, you know, most companies, if you look at how they plan, they plan on an annual cycle. They say, hey, they're going to do an annual operating plan, these are the budgets, these are the things that we're going to do. Um, with AI and the progress that we're making through AI adoption, uh, throughout the industry, uh, what we're seeing is what used to be, let's call it, you know, fairly static plans, are now actually becoming pretty dynamic. Um, you're not realizing how fast the adoption curve is going. You you actually see an opportunity like I said, with you know, muse is one of the best examples. I mean, over 10 million people activating in the span of 45 days. I mean, that's pretty incredible. Like that's that's a adoption curve that uh, you know, probably wasn't in the regular plan. And we're seeing that across a number of applications. And so from our standpoint, uh we are uh very dynamic. You know, we're a tech company that has um a lot of resources and the ability to uh expand our supply and expand our ability to help our customers. And that's what's led to, you know, tremendous growth. So, uh being able to say that my data center business is going to grow 50% sequentially from Q3 to Q4, uh it's a big step up and it's a a testament to how important computing is um in the industry today and you know, we're looking to double the business, more than double the business as we go into next year. Uh we are a data center first company, that is um our profile and you know, people need more computing to power all these applications. 
 02:40 Brian I don't want this to sound like me, I don't want this to appear like, you know, I've lost my mind because but because I haven't. But is this a starting point when you say your business could double next year and your revenues are can go up significantly. Is that just your starting point? If the business is that dynamic, I mean, can we have this conversation a year from now and you will have raised guidance a few more times? 
 03:09 Lisa Well, it's certainly always our intention to, you know, continue to meet the needs of the business. Um I look at it as uh we are extremely ambitious, Brian, in terms of what we want to do, what we want to do with our customers. Um this is an opportunity for us to be like I want to be the best partner uh to uh the largest users of compute in the world. And sure, I mean, we we see lots of opportunity for, you know, continued acceleration of the business. Obviously, we have to go through uh you know, each quarter, quarter by quarter, but we're planning for success and I think we've had um a decent uh track record at that. 
 04:08 Brian I've spent the past month of my life, Lisa, writing about Core Weve, bond yields. I didn't really didn't want to do that. I got sucked into it. I had to do it. I I'm writing about companies and hyperscalers having their stocks get hit because of concerns about free cash flow. Is the market right to question the growth of AI? 
 04:41 Lisa I would say it this way, Brian. I think the market can sometimes be a little bit short-sighted, uh and look, it it is what it is. Um, what I look at is in the long term, if you believe, which I do. I believe, uh, very, you know, deeply that computing in many ways equates to intelligence. So the more compute you have, the more intelligent you are, the more intelligent your company is, the more problems you're going to be able to solve, the more you're going to accelerate your business. If you believe that foundation, then inven- investing ahead of the curve is the right thing to do because we're always investing for the long term. Long term being, you know, three, five, four, five years and beyond. And that means you have to make the investments now. So, I think from our standpoint, I've always operated AMD that way. We're always looking at, you know, what do we see over the horizon? And over the horizon, I see um AI and super intelligence becoming more and more essential to every aspect of our lives and every aspect of our business. So I believe in this demand and I very much believe that uh you know, many of the investments that are being made throughout the ecosystem are also seeing some of these, you know, same trends.
